gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: Antares Syndicate 1274 experienced a strengthening of prior year reserves by $9.890 million in 2017. This deterioration in net provision for claims outstanding at the previous year end (2016) was primarily due to adverse claims development and IBNR recalibration. The year 2017 was marked by significant catastrophe events including Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, and Maria (total net loss $51m), Californian Wildfires, Mexican and New Zealand Earthquakes, Peru Flooding, and Tropical Storm Lidia, which heavily impacted the Property, Marine, Aviation and Transport (MAT), and Reinsurance divisions. Additionally, a Brazilian plane crash and the sinking of the Stellar Daisy cargo ship and Seikongen fishing vessel contributed to losses in the Aviation and Hull classes respectively.

gpt-5-mini.standardized_narrative: The syndicate opened 2017 with gross claims outstanding of $527.6m. During the year the net provision for prior years deteriorated by $9.89m (approximately 1.87% of opening gross claims), reflecting adverse prior-year development primarily driven by deterioration/IBNR adjustments and large loss development. The 2017 hurricane season (Harvey, Irma, Maria) and other natural catastrophes materially affected Property, Marine and Reinsurance portfolios; Irma was the largest single event for the syndicate. Prior-year reserve movements were disclosed as a net deterioration; no comprehensive per-LOB prior-year reserve breakdown was provided.
